claims: Artemis I was an uncrewed flight testing SLS and Orion systems.
Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026 from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II marks the first crewed flight around the Moon since 1972.
Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
Artemis II is a crewed mission for lunar fly-by and return.
Artemis II's crew includes Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
Artemis II's flight path includes launch, earth orbit tests, trans-lunar injection, lunar flyby, and Pacific splashdown.
Artemis III is scheduled for mid-2027.
Artemis III is the first crewed mission to land on the lunar surface.
Artemis IV is scheduled for early 2028.
Artemis IV involves further crewed lunar landings.
Artemis V is scheduled for late 2028.
Artemis V is a subsequent crewed landing mission.
